description: Public documentation/interoperability vectors, not runtime implementation or provider qualification. Ephemeral independent publisher/verifier Ed25519 keys were generated once, and regenerated after the 2026-11-06 gap review (canonical policy digests, per-check digest rules, provider_package_fingerprint coverage, challenge issued_at, strict-verification negatives including canonical small-order R, cache deadlines and status generation advancement); only public JWKs and signatures are retained. No private seed is retained. All identities, service observations and policy inputs are fictional. Positive assessment is declaration-only, never official installed-code proof. Base positive is a production Axum declaration using dns-key-control-v1 in explicitly isolated synthetic protocol context. Optional fingerprint and official-shaped objects contain fictional methods/releases/digests; production_provider_qualification=false. No production provider method is qualified by these vectors.
encoding: JWS signing input is ASCII protected_segment + dot + payload_segment. Verify those exact segments. JSON bytes use sorted keys and compact ASCII-compatible serialization; fixture values use the RFC 8785-compatible integer/ASCII subset. Digests of signed objects hash exact compact ASCII bytes.
validation_order: 1 bounded strict JSON/JWS decode with duplicate rejection
2 protected header, expected message type and trusted issuer key
4 payload schema and cross-field consistency, including per-check digest rules
5 issuer, policy id/version/digest and method allowlists
6 time: issuance skew, exclusive expiry, observation age
7 exact host, environment and binding equality with fresh evidence
8 result against the policy's required checks
Verifier-issuance cases (operator authorization, durable state, signer fencing) are preconditions checked by the verifier, not consumer inputs.

Default require_status=false accepts while assessment remains valid under the isolated synthetic declaration policy.
Signature scalar S replaced by S + L. Non-strict verifiers may accept it; strict verification (parent PA-WIRE) must reject it.
Public key is a small-order point. Reject at discovery, enrollment and verification.
Uppercase host and trailing slash: not a canonical HTTPS identifier, and not an alias of the canonical form.

Canonical R encodes the identity point; A is canonical and non-small-order, and S is canonical. Ordinary cofactorless Ed25519 verification may accept this signature; the strict profile rejects small-order R.

A newly accepted binding advances the enrollment generation and public sequence without withdrawing the still-valid prior assessment. Fresh current status for that prior binding uses the new sequence.
Once sequence 2 is observed, the earlier sequence 1 response is rejected even if its time window has not expired.
Observation age starts at observed_from, not evaluated_at.
Required-status freshness starts at the status issued_at, not evaluated_at.
A configured cache lifetime starts at evaluated_at; rereading a cache never restarts it.
Local trust-key acceptance may stop before the verifier-published key validity; this local deadline caps caching without changing the signed assessment expiry.
A result is no longer current at observed_from plus the configured maximum age.
Required status is too old at issued_at plus the configured maximum age, even before its signed expires_at.
Evidence issued 31 seconds after the consumer clock exceeds the allowed 30-second future-issuance skew.

Local cache-state trace, not a wire object: a previously validated live-mode result records sequence 1 for its supporting issuer/enrollment. Learning sequence 2 invalidates that cached result at time 3610, before valid_until 3659; fresh sequence-2 support is required before accepting again.
